mainTopic: The end of the ramp-murder story, and the garments and status of the כהן who removes and carries out the ashes
overview: This amud finishes the story of the כהן who was stabbed on the ramp of the מזבח. The גמרא shows that רבי צדוק's mention of עגלה ערופה cannot be meant literally: ירושלים never brings one, and the killer was known. So he said it only to make the people cry. The story continues with the father, who cared more that the knife stay טהור than about his dying son. A פסוק about מנשה shows that the problem was that murder had become cheap in their eyes. The גמרא then returns to the ashes of the מזבח. A ברייתא teaches that the clothes worn to carry the ashes out are still holy but plainer, and רבי אליעזר learns that בעלי מומין may carry them out. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about whether this dispute also covers הרמת הדשן, and they read the פסוק's mention of only two garments in different ways. Finally, the גמרא suggests their argument matches an older dispute between רבי יהודה, רבי דוסא and רבי about the extra word ילבש. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ירושלים never brings an עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the quoted ברייתא state that ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה. This undercuts רבי צדוק's suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: ירושלים does not bring an עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about special rules for ירושלים. Its final rule is that ירושלים never brings an עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי צדוק had asked whether the city or the עזרה should bring the עגלה ערופה. But this ברייתא says ירושלים is excluded from that מצוה altogether. So taken literally, his suggestion cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken, brought when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a quote that started earlier. It is the ending of the source being used to challenge רבי צדוק, not a brand-new statement.

phrases.english: [Jerusalem] does not bring an eglah arufah.
phrases.notes: This is the last item in the list of special laws for Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא cited on the previous amud as a challenge to רבי צדוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי צדוק's call to bring an עגלה ערופה for the murder in the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ירושלים is exempt from עגלה ערופה, so the suggestion cannot be meant literally

steps.title: A second problem: the killer was known
steps.stepSummary: The תורה requires an עגלה ערופה only when the killer is unknown. Here everyone saw who did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the verse says 'it is not known who struck him.' But here it was known who struck him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why an עגלה ערופה cannot apply. The פסוק limits it to an unknown killer, and here the killer was known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first problem was about the place, ירושלים. This problem is about the case itself. Even outside ירושלים, a known killer means no עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not known who struck him (דברים כא:א)

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is written: 'It is not known who struck him,'
phrases.notes: This is a condition the פסוק about עגלה ערופה sets.

phrases.english: but here it was known who struck him!
phrases.notes: The other כהן was seen stabbing him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent objection
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי צדוק's mention of עגלה ערופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires an unknown killer, and this killer was known

steps.title: He said it only to make people cry
steps.stepSummary: רבי צדוק did not mean that an עגלה ערופה was required. He mentioned it to stir up mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said it in order to increase the weeping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both problems. רבי צדוק was not giving a הלכה. He was trying to make the people feel how terrible the murder was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By comparing the killing to the case of a corpse found in a field, he made the crowd feel shame and grief. The words were a speech, not a ruling, so neither objection applies.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי צדוק's mention of עגלה ערופה was a rebuke meant to bring out grief, not a הלכה.

phrases.english: Rather, [he said it] in order to increase the weeping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves both objections
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the statement as a speech meant to move people, not a legal ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי צדוק meant that an עגלה ערופה must actually be brought
steps.terutzMaskana: He only wanted to increase weeping

steps.title: The father's shocking words
steps.stepSummary: The story continues. The father finds his son still alive and calls him their כפרה, yet worries only about the knife staying pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The boy's father came and found him still convulsing. He said: 'He is your atonement. My son is still alive,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the story. The father sees his son is not yet dead and says the knife has not become טמא, since a corpse has not yet touched it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of his words: the knife is still pure. His concern is to remove the knife before the boy dies so it will not become טמא מת. Saving his son, or mourning him, is not his focus.

phrases.english: The father of the boy came
phrases.notes: The young victim was also a כהן

phrases.english: and found him while he was still convulsing.
He said: 'He is your atonement,
and my son is still alive,' etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the quote: so the knife has not become impure

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא אָבִיו שֶׁל תִּינוֹק וּמְצָאוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא מְפַרְפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father cared that the knife stay טהור while his son was still alive

steps.title: The lesson: purity mattered more to them than life
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states the moral of the story: they took טהרת כלים more seriously than שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches you that the purity of vessels was more serious to them than bloodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the story was told. It shows that the people's priorities had become twisted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is criticism, not praise. The father's worry about the knife shows that, for them, purity of utensils outweighed a human life. This statement sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: To teach you that the purity of vessels was more serious to them
than bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁקָּשָׁה עֲלֵיהֶם טׇהֳרַת כֵּלִים יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the moral from the father's words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They valued טהרת כלים above שפיכות דמים

steps.title: Which value went out of balance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: did murder become cheap to them, or did purity become exaggerated?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Had bloodshed become cheap, while purity of vessels stayed where it was? Or perhaps bloodshed stayed where it was, but purity of vessels had become overly strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly the ברייתא's criticism means. Two possible problems could each produce the same imbalance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: they cared too little about murder, and purity was valued normally. Option two: they valued murder normally, but blew up the importance of purity. Either way purity ends up 'higher,' so the גמרא wants to know which side moved.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Was it bloodshed that became cheap,
but purity of vessels stayed where it was?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים — כִּדְקָיְימָא קָיְימָא,
phrases.english: Or perhaps bloodshed stayed where it was,
but it was purity of vessels that became overly strict?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים הוּא דְּזָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a more exact reading of the ברייתא's lesson
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the imbalance came from devaluing murder or from overvaluing purity

steps.title: The verse about מנשה shows murder had become cheap
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק about מנשה spilling innocent blood. This shows the problem was that murder had become cheap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: since the teaching cites 'And also מנשה spilled innocent blood,' learn from this that bloodshed became cheap, while purity of vessels stayed where it was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק the ברייתא attached to the story. A פסוק about the sin of murder points to the failure being in how they treated murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the problem been too much stress on purity, the ברייתא would not cite a פסוק about bloodshed. Citing the sin of מנשה shows that the blame lies with treating murder lightly. The value they placed on purity was normal.

keyTerms.meaning: It cites a teaching (a פסוק) for it

steps.whatToRemember: The sin was that murder had become cheap in their eyes. Caring about טהרת כלים was not itself the problem.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, מִדְּקָא נָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear: since the teaching adduces for it a verse:
'And also innocent blood Menashe spilled,'

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים הוּא דְּזָל,
phrases.english: learn from this that it was bloodshed that became cheap,
and purity of vessels stayed where it was.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, מִדְּקָא נָסֵיב לַהּ תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Murder had become cheap, and the value placed on purity was unchanged

steps.title: Changing clothes to take out the ashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins explaining the פסוק about changing garments before carrying out the ashes. Its first suggestion compares it to יום הכפורים: removing holy clothes and putting on ordinary ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: 'And he shall take off his garments and put on other garments and carry out the ashes.' I might understand this like the practice of יום הכפורים, where he takes off holy garments and puts on non-holy garments,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic of the work with the ashes. It begins a ברייתא that first offers a possible reading of 'other garments.' This is a setup, and the ברייתא will refine it in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שׁוֹמְעַנִי' marks an initial assumption that will likely be corrected. The first idea is that, as on יום הכפורים, the change is from בגדי קודש to בגדי חול. The ברייתא's final answer comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: 'שׁוֹמְעַנִי' is not the final ruling. It is only a first guess that the ברייתא is about to adjust.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And he shall take off [his garments] and put on other garments
and carry out the ashes,'
I might understand it like the manner of Yom Kippur,
where he takes off sacred garments
and puts on non-sacred garments,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וּפָשַׁט וְלָבַשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים וְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַדֶּשֶׁן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the laws of the ashes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: 'other garments' means ordinary clothes, as on יום הכפורים

steps.title: The verse shows the new clothes are also sacred
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the יום הכפורים comparison. It uses a היקש to show that the clothes the כהן puts on are also בגדי קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'He shall take off his garments and put on other garments.' It compares the clothes he puts on to the clothes he takes off. Just as the clothes he takes off are sacred, so too the clothes he puts on are sacred.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own first suggestion from step 8, which said he changes into ordinary clothes like on יום הכפורים. It proves from the verse that the new clothes are also holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions taking off and putting on in one breath, so the two sets of clothes are linked. Since the first set is clearly בגדי קודש, the second set must be too. This cancels the idea that he switches to ordinary clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. This introduces a verse that settles the question.
Compares or links two things in a verse (הֶקֵּשׁ) so they share the same law
Just as there, so too here. This is the standard wording of a comparison.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two steps. In step 8 the ברייתא only suggested ordinary clothes as a possibility. Here it rejects that suggestion, and the conclusion is that both sets of clothes are holy.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And he shall take off his garments
and put on other garments"
it compares the garments he puts on
to the garments he takes off
just as there they are sacred garments,
so too here they are sacred garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וּפָשַׁט אֶת בְּגָדָיו וְלָבַשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the יום הכפורים suggestion from step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the second set of clothes is ordinary (חול)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse links the two sets of clothes, so the second set must also be sacred

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'other' clothes?
steps.stepSummary: If both sets of clothes are sacred, the ברייתא asks what the word אחרים adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'other' clothes?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about the word אחרים. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'other' suggests the second set is different from the first. Now that both sets are holy, we need to know how they are different.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This means: given what we just concluded.

phrases.english: If so,
why does the verse say "other"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word אחרים means, given the conclusion of step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What difference does אחרים point to if both sets of clothes are sacred?

steps.title: The other clothes are of lower quality
steps.stepSummary: The answer: אחרים means the second set of clothes is less fine than the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are of lower quality than the first ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The 'other' clothes are still sacred, but they are not as fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sets stay בגדי קודש, as step 9 proved. The difference is only in quality: carrying the ashes outside is a dirtier job, so he wears less fine clothes for it.

phrases.english: Of lower quality than them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחרים means the clothes are of lesser quality, but they are still sacred

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: blemished כהנים may carry out the ashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads אחרים together with the next word, והוציא. He learns that בעלי מומין are allowed to carry out the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'Other... and he shall carry out.' This teaches that כהנים with blemishes are allowed to carry out the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a different meaning for the word אחרים. For him it describes other people, not other clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He connects אחרים to והוציא. This means 'others' may do the carrying out: blemished כהנים, who normally cannot serve. So for him, הוצאת הדשן is a job that even בעלי מומין may do.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים with physical blemishes, who normally may not do the Temple service
Allowed or valid to do something
Carrying the ashes out of the camp

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Other... and he shall carry out"
this teaches about blemished priests
that they are allowed to carry out the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of אחרים from the one in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blemished כהנים may carry out the ashes

steps.title: Support for 'lower quality' from דבי רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the view that the clothes are 'lower quality.' It points to a teaching from דבי רבי ישמעאל about a servant's clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Other' means of lower quality. This matches what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: the clothes a servant wore while cooking a pot for his master should not be worn when he pours a cup of wine for his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now comments on the ברייתא. It explains why dirty work calls for different, lesser clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A servant who cooked got his clothes dirty, so he should not serve his master a drink in them. In the same way, the כהן should not wear his finer clothes for the messy job of carrying the ashes outside. This is a matter of respect, not a question of holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. This introduces a line quoted from the ברייתא for discussion.
As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught

steps.whatToRemember: The second set of clothes is still holy. It is only plainer, out of respect, because carrying out the ashes is dirty work.

phrases.english: The Master said:
"Other" means of lower quality than them,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.
For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
clothes in which he cooked a pot for his master
he should not pour a cup for his master in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אֲחֵרִים פְּחוּתִין מֵהֶן, כִּדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the answer in step 11 and gives it a source
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the second set of clothes is of lower quality
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל about a servant's cooking clothes

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the argument also covers removing the ashes from the altar
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the מחלוקת about בעלי מומין applies both to carrying the ashes out (הוצאה) and to removing them from the altar (הרמה).
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: just as there is a dispute about carrying the ashes out, so there is a dispute about removing the ashes from the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר goes. ריש לקיש says it covers both jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, רבי אליעזר would allow בעלי מומין even to do the הרמה at the altar, and the תנא קמא would forbid both jobs. So the two jobs follow the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש
Carrying the ashes out of the camp
Removing a portion of the ashes from the altar (תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different jobs. הרמה is taking ashes off the altar, which is the morning service. הוצאה is carrying the piled-up ashes outside the camp. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Just as there is a dispute about carrying out,
so there is a dispute about removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כְּמַחְלוֹקֶת בְּהוֹצָאָה, כָּךְ מַחְלוֹקֶת בַּהֲרָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how far the dispute in step 12 reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about בעלי מומין applies to both הוצאה and הרמה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: removing the ashes is a true Temple service for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument is only about carrying the ashes out. Everyone agrees that הרמה is a real עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the dispute is about carrying out. But removal from the altar is a Temple service according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with ריש לקיש about how wide the argument is. For him, it is limited to הוצאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since הרמה is a true עבודה, even רבי אליעזר agrees that בעלי מומין may not do it. רבי אליעזר's leniency applies only to carrying the ashes outside.

keyTerms.meaning: A true Temple service, which needs a fit כהן

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says the argument about בעלי מומין covers both הוצאה and הרמה. רבי יוחנן says only הוצאה is argued about. For him הרמה is a real עבודה according to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question of whether הרמת הדשן counts as a full עבודה, like the other services that need a fit כהן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
the dispute is about carrying out,
but regarding removal
everyone agrees it is a Temple service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּהוֹצָאָה, אֲבָל בַּהֲרָמָה דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל עֲבוֹדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש's view of how wide the dispute is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about הוצאה; all agree that הרמה is an עבודה, which בעלי מומין may not perform

steps.title: What is ריש לקיש's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש holds that the מחלוקת also applies to הרמה, meaning that even removing the ashes is not a full עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind ריש לקיש's opinion from Step 14. This is a setup line. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees that הרמה is a real עבודה. ריש לקיש disagreed. The גמרא now wants to know what made ריש לקיש doubt that הרמה is a real עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל who often argues with רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: What is the reason of Reish Lakish?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the opinion stated in Step 14, which רבי יוחנן disputed in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic that leads ריש לקיש to say that הרמה is also not a full עבודה.

steps.title: No real service is done in only two garments
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's reason: the פסוק mentions only two garments, and no true עבודה can be done with just two garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: If you think removing the ashes is a real עבודה, is there any עבודה that may be done wearing only two garments?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש. The פסוק about the ashes mentions only two garments, but every real עבודה needs the full set of four. So removing the ashes cannot be a real עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן wears four garments for every עבודה. The פסוק (ויקרא ו:ג) names only מדו בד and מכנסי בד. ריש לקיש reads this literally: only two garments are needed. So the side that allows בעלי מומין (רבי אליעזר) can hold that even הרמה is not a full עבודה, which is why the מחלוקת reaches הרמה too.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

steps.confusionAlert: Here כֵלִים does not mean vessels or utensils. It means garments, the priestly clothing.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
If it enters your mind that it is a real Temple service,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁכְּשֵׁירָה בִּשְׁנֵי כֵלִים?
phrases.english: do you have any service that is valid with only two garments?
phrases.notes: The פסוק: "ולבש הכהן מדו בד ומכנסי בד ילבש על בשרו"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ עֲבוֹדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the Torah lists only two garments, the act cannot be a full עבודה, because every real עבודה needs four garments.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the two garments are examples for all four
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that all four garments are required. The Torah named the tunic and pants, and the same applies to the turban and belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן? The Torah revealed this about the tunic and pants, and the same law applies to the turban and the belt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן deals with the פסוק that mentions only two garments. He says the Torah mentioned two, but it really means all four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, הרמה is a real עבודה, so it needs all four garments. The Torah named two garments to show that priestly clothing is required here, not ordinary clothes. The other two garments are included automatically (והוא הדין).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan (how does he explain it)?
The Torah revealed it regarding the tunic and the pants,
and the same is true for the turban and the belt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בְּכֻתּוֹנֶת וּמִכְנָסַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reading of the same פסוק that ריש לקיש used in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two garments in the פסוק are examples. All four are really required.

steps.title: Then why name just these two?
steps.stepSummary: Against רבי יוחנן: if all four garments are needed, why does the Torah mention only the tunic and the pants?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about these two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. If all four garments are required, the Torah should not single out two. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן's view, naming only two garments looks unnecessary or even misleading. The גמרא demands a reason for choosing these two specifically.

phrases.english: And what is different about these two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given for רבי יוחנן in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two garments are only examples for all four.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all four are required, the Torah would not single out two unless they teach something special.

steps.title: Each named garment teaches its own law
steps.stepSummary: The tunic is called מדו to teach that it must fit exactly. The pants are named to teach that they must be put on first.
steps.simpleTranslation: "His linen garment (מדו)": מדו means it must be according to his size. "Linen pants" teaches what was taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that no garment should be put on before the pants? As it says, "and his linen pants he shall put on his flesh."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each of the two named garments comes to teach a separate law. That is why only these two were singled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word מדו ("his measure") teaches that the tunic must be tailored to the כהן's size. The pants are mentioned together with "on his flesh" to show they go on first, when nothing is yet on his body. So the mention of the two garments is not wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: "His linen garment":
"middo" means according to his size (it must fit him exactly).
"Linen pants" comes for that which was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר קוֹדֶם לַמִּכְנָסַיִם,
phrases.english: From where do we know that no garment should come before the pants?
As it says: "And his linen pants he shall put on his flesh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each named garment is needed for a separate דרשה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming only two garments seems pointless if all four are required.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two garments were named to teach two laws: the tunic must fit, and the pants go on first.

steps.title: Where does ריש לקיש learn these laws?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש uses the mention of two garments to show that only two are worn. So where does he learn the fit rule and the pants-first rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to ריש לקיש. He already used the two named garments for his own point, so he needs another source for these two laws. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the Torah named two garments because only two are actually worn. That means he cannot use the naming of the garments to teach the two extra laws. The גמרא asks what his source is.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish (from where does he learn these laws)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 20 gave רבי יוחנן's sources, the גמרא asks how ריש לקיש gets the same laws.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: ריש לקיש's sources for the fit rule and the pants-first rule.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns both laws from the wording
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the fit rule from the unusual word מדו, and the pants-first rule from the words על בשרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: "According to his size": he learns it from the fact that the Torah used the word מדו. "No garment before the pants": that comes from "on his flesh."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש can also learn both laws, but from the specific wording of the פסוק rather than from the fact that the two garments were named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have said כתונת but chose the word מדו, and that word choice teaches the fit rule. The added phrase על בשרו teaches that the pants go directly on his bare body, so they come first. So both opinions keep both laws, just from different parts of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: It expressed it (the Torah phrased it)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: only two garments are named, so הרמה can be seen as less than a full עבודה, and the מחלוקת about בעלי מומין applies to it too. רבי יוחנן: all four garments are needed, so הרמה is a full עבודה according to everyone, and the two named garments teach extra laws. Both agree that the tunic must fit and that the pants go on first. They differ only on where those laws come from.

phrases.english: The law that the tunic must be according to his size:
he learns it from the fact that the Torah expressed it with the word "middo."
The law that no garment should come before the pants:
is derived from the words "on his flesh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 and finishes the comparison of the two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fit rule comes from the word מדו. The pants-first rule comes from על בשרו.

steps.title: Proposing that the dispute matches an older argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute parallels a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה learns from the extra word 'ילבש' that the turban and belt are worn for הרמת הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like an argument between תנאים. The verse could have said only 'on his flesh', so why does it add 'shall he put on'? To include the turban and the belt for the removal of the ashes. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the argument we just learned is really an older argument between תנאים. It begins quoting a ברייתא, starting with רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא ו:ג seems to say 'ילבש' one time too many. רבי יהודה reads that extra word as adding the מצנפת and אבנט to the garments worn for הרמת הדשן. This sounds just like רבי יוחנן, who requires all four garments.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like (a dispute of) תנאים. The גמרא proposes that an אמוראים dispute matches an older one.
Why does the verse need to say this? Asked when a word looks extra.
To include. The extra word adds something new.
The turban of a כהן הדיוט
The belt or sash of a כהן
The removal of the ashes from the altar (תרומת הדשן)

steps.confusionAlert: 'נימא' means 'let us say'. It is only a suggestion. The גמרא has not yet decided that these תנאים really match רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of Tannaim:
phrases.notes: The גמרא proposes a parallel to the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute.

phrases.english: [The verse could have said only] "on his flesh";
why does the verse say "shall he put on"?
To include the turban and the belt for the removal [of the ashes];
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both אמוראים have been shown to account for the verse's details, the גמרא looks for an earlier tannaic source behind their dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute is an older dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the extra word 'ילבש' in ויקרא ו:ג, beginning with רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי דוסא reads the extra word as permitting the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים clothes for a כהן הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא uses 'ילבש' to teach a different law: the linen garments the כהן גדול wore on יום הכיפורים may later be used by a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא says: the word comes to include the clothes of the כהן גדול from יום הכיפורים. They are fit to be worn by an ordinary כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second opinion. רבי דוסא uses the same extra word for a completely different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא does not use 'ילבש' to add the turban and belt. He uses it to teach that the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים garments do not have to be put away forever. According to the גמרא's suggestion (נימא), since the word is used up for this, he would have no source for four garments at הרמת הדשן, which would seem to fit ריש לקיש. The גמרא has not yet confirmed this match.

keyTerms.meaning: To include or add. This works like לְהָבִיא.
The garments of the כהן גדול. Here, his white linen garments of יום הכיפורים.
An ordinary כהן who is not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says:
To include the garments of the High Priest
on Yom Kippur,
that they are fit for an ordinary priest.
phrases.notes: They may be reused in regular service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second opinion in the same ברייתא. It uses the same word differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים linen garments may afterward be used by a כהן הדיוט. This is learned from 'ילבש'.

steps.title: רבי gives two refutations of רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רבי objects to רבי דוסא in two ways. First, the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים belt is different from an ordinary כהן's belt. Second, garments used for a higher holiness should not be used for a lower holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: there are two answers against this. One: the belt of the כהן גדול is not the same as the belt of an ordinary כהן. And also: clothes you used for a very serious holiness, would you then use them for a lighter holiness?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) argues against רבי דוסא's reading and gives two reasons why it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: on יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול's belt is pure linen. In רבי's view, an ordinary כהן's belt is wool and linen, so the set cannot simply pass to a כהן הדיוט. Reason two: clothes used for the holiest service of the year should not be lowered to ordinary service. So 'ילבש' cannot mean what רבי דוסא said.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this matter
Severe or higher holiness. Here, the יום הכיפורים service.
Lighter holiness. Here, ordinary daily service.

steps.whyThisMatters: The second argument states a general principle: something used for a higher holiness should not be lowered to a lesser use.

phrases.english: Rebbi said: There are two refutations of this matter:
One: that the belt of the High Priest
phrases.notes: His יום הכיפורים belt is pure linen.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of an ordinary priest.
phrases.notes: In רבי's view, the ordinary belt is wool and linen.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד: בְּגָדִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּמַּשְׁתָּ בָּהֶן קְדוּשָּׁה חֲמוּרָה,
phrases.english: And furthermore: garments with which you performed a service of severe holiness,
will you use them for a service of lighter holiness?!
phrases.notes: He's asking this to make a point: surely not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step attacks רבי דוסא's reading from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי דוסא's reading that 'ילבש' permits the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים garments for a כהן הדיוט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First, the garments are not identical, because the belts are made of different materials. Second, it is improper to lower clothes from a higher holiness to a lower one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי דוסא's reading that 'ילבש' permits the כהן גדול's יום הכיפורים garments for a כהן הדיוט
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The belts are not identical, and garments used for a higher holiness may not be lowered to a lesser holiness.

steps.title: רבי reopens the question of what the extra word teaches
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected רבי דוסא, רבי asks again what 'ילבש' comes to teach. The answer comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the verse say 'shall he put on'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Since רבי has rejected רבי דוסא's reading, he asks again what the extra word means, and his own answer is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' signals that the old explanation is gone and a replacement is needed. The question stays open here and is answered right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather or instead. It signals a replacement for a rejected idea.
'Shall he put on.' This is the extra word being explained.

phrases.english: Rather, why does the verse say "shall he put on"?
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After refuting רבי דוסא, רבי opens his own explanation of the word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'ילבש' teaches, now that רבי דוסא's reading has been rejected
